Date March 28 1931.

Subject (in full) Woo Shing Book Store (華興書局), No. 763 Connaught Road.

Made by D. I. Ross Forwarded by [Signature] 3.1.

With reference to a previous report dated March 4,
1931, on the subject of the above, Sung Yung-fong (沈芳芳),
the occupant of the room which was searched for communistic
literature on the authority of a warrant, issued at the
instance of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, on March 1,
returned to that address during the night of March 17/18.
She was subsequently interviewed and a statement which was
taken from her is attached herewith. While being cognizant
of the existence of the Woo Shing Book Store (華興書局), she
denies ever having taken any interest in its activities.
Appended also is a statement obtained from
Wong Foh-keng (王福慶), the proprietor of the tea leaf shop
which occupies the ground floor of No. 763 Connaught Road.

D.I.W.
D. I.
D.C. (Cr. & Sp. Branches)

C. D. J. Robertson,
Can anything further be
done in this matter at present?
[Signature]
28.3.31.

Nothing further can be done at present.
The woman Sung Yung-fong has
given up the tenancy of the room at
763 Connaught Road and it is believed
returned to her home in Szechuan
File [Signature] 30.3.31.
HR
26/3/31

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of Sung Yung-fong (沈榮芳 ).
native of Szechuen taken by me D. I. Ross
at on the 10/3/31 and interpreted by D. L. Sih Tse-liang

My name is Sung Yung-fong. I am a native of Pa Hsien
(巴縣), Szechuen, age 17 and single. I arrived in Shanghai
some ten months ago and since that time have resided at
765 Connaught Road. My object in coming to Shanghai was to
study but so far I have been unable to gain admission into
any school. On February 28, 1931, I left 765 Connaught Road
to see my cousin named Chang Zoong-yung (張仲容) who resided
at 482 Manila Road. Here I stayed until the following day,
March 1. While I was returning home, I was stopped at Carter
and Sinza Roads corner by the daughter of the sub-tenant of
765 Connaught Road, named Wong Sieu-tsung (瑪貞), who told
me that my room had been raided by a foreigner from the Police
Station. As there were certain books in my room which had
been left there by the Woo Shing Book Store, when it occupied 762
Connaught Road, the next house, and fearing that the nature of
these books, although I had no knowledge of their contents,
might incriminate me, I was afraid to go to 765 Connaught Road,
and therefore went to stay with my cousin at 482 Manila Road.
I lived here until March 17 when my cousin departed for Szechuen.
On the night of March 17 I returned to 765 Connaught Road to
change my clothing. The chop of the Woo Shing Book Store
(華興書局) was left in my room by my male cousin named Li
Shiao-sien (李孝先), who was formerly in the employ of the
Woo Shing Book Store when it was located at 762 Connaught
Road. I do not know the present whereabouts of the Woo Shing
Book Store. A fellow worker of my cousins' named Koong(農)
used to visit 765 Connaught Road and collect any books and

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警方调查报告。
以下为沈荣芳（Sung Yung-fong），四川籍人士，于31年3月10日由我，警探长罗斯（D. I. Ross）在______取得，并由翻译员施子良（D. L. Sih Tse-liang）翻译的供词。

我叫沈荣芳。我是四川巴县（Pa Hsien）人，年龄17岁，未婚。我大约十个月前抵达上海，此后一直居住在康纳路765号。我来上海的目的是求学，但至今未能进入任何学校。1931年2月28日，我离开康纳路765号，去探望住在马尼拉路482号的表亲张仲容（Chang Zoong-yung）。我在此住到次日，即3月1日。在我回家途中，在卡特路与新闸路转角处，被康纳路765号二房东的女儿玛贞（Wong Sieu-tsung）拦住，她告诉我我的房间被一名来自巡捕房的外国人搜查了。由于我的房间里有一些书籍，是隔壁康纳路762号的华兴书局在那里时留下的，虽然我不知晓这些书的内容，但我担心这些书的性质可能会连累我，因此不敢回康纳路765号，于是去马尼拉路482号与表亲同住。我在此居住至3月17日，当时我的表亲启程前往四川。3月17日晚，我回到康纳路765号更换衣物。华兴书局（Woo Shing Book Store）的印章是我的表亲李孝先（Li Shiao-sien）留在我房间的，他曾在华兴书局位于康纳路762号时受雇于该局。我不知道华兴书局目前的下落。我表亲的一位同事农（Koong）常来康纳路765号收取寄给

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of Wong Foh-kong (王福康)
native of ____________________ taken by me D.I.Ross
at ______________ on the 10/5/31 and interpreted by D.I.Lim Tee-liang

My name is Wong Foh-kong (王福康). I am the proprietor
of a book shop at 769 Nanking Road. All mail matters
addressed to the Woo Shing Book Store (華興書局) were handled
by the cousin of Sung Hung-fong (沈榮芳) prior to November,
1930 and after that time she took charge of all correspondence.
The chop "Receipt of the Woo Shing Book Store", was left there
by her cousin who was once an employee of this book store
when it occupied the adjoining premises 762 Nanking Road.
A certain individual named Young occasionally called and took away
the mail matter.

警方调查报告。
以下为王福康（Wong Foh-kong），______籍人士，于31年5月10日由我，警探长罗斯（D.I.Ross）在______________取得，并由翻译员林梯良（D.I.Lim Tee-liang）翻译的供词。

我叫王福康（Wong Foh-kong）。我是南京路769号一家书店的店主。1930年11月之前，所有寄给华兴书局（Woo Shing Book Store）的邮件均由沈荣芳（Sung Hung-fong，原文如此，应为沈荣芳或沈芳芳）的表亲处理，此后则由她负责所有信件往来。“华兴书局收讫”印章是由她的表亲留下的，他曾在该书店位于隔壁南京路762号时受雇于此。一个名叫杨（Young）的人偶尔会来取走邮件。

Subject (in full) Observation on the Book Store, 765 Connaught Road

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE & S.D. REGISTER No. S. B. D. 2048 Date 10 3 31）

Made by Forwarded by

Sir,

Reference to the Book Store situated at 765 Connaught Road, observation has been maintained at the above place, since 1/3/31 in accordance with instruction received from D.I. Ross of Special Branch, but nothing has eventuated. The proprietor has failed to return and the place still remains closed. Two letters were delivered to the above address and seized by the detectives posted on duty. These two letters were later forwarded to D.I. Ross of the Special Branch and are in his possession.

The detective on the section in which 765 Connaught Road is situated has been instructed to pay daily visits to the above premises in case of further developments.

（批：attached to file）

Officer i/c.
Special Branch.

SI,
For comment please.
J.R.
10:3:31.
Supt. (detn),
Please dispose.
J.R.
11:3:31.

Further watch on this house is not likely to bring results. I suggest the search warrant, together with the wooden chop referred to in report by D.I. Ross (Flag "A") and a note to the effect that pur watch has proved abortive, be returned to Supt. Whiting.
J Robertson
Supt. 11.3.31.

1931, enquiries made by the Police on March 5 at No.1186 S Wen Li

with the latter named book store.

The premises in question is a Chinese dwelling house,
and is occupied by five families of the working class.

page_data.en:
Translation of a letter dated February 27, 1931,
from the Woo Shing Book Store (華興書局), 763
Connaught Road, addressed to Loo Jen-wei (羅仁偉),
Sing Tai Ziang Shop (新泰祥), 209 Chung Hwa
Sing Road, Chapei.

------------------

Li. Loo Jen-wei:

You stated that you wanted to purchase our
books but did not know where you could get them, for
which we are exceedingly sorry. But if you
consider that the address you sent us is a place
where we can mail the books, we will then do at once.
We are very grateful to you for your suggestion to
establish a private agency to sell our books. Please
appoint a time and place so as to enable us to send
somebody to see you when we can discuss matters.
May we expect your reply at once? You may send
your letter to the same place as you did last time.

Awaiting anxiously your reply.

The Shanghai Woo Shing Book Store.

2/27
page_data.zh:
1931年2月27日，由康纳路763号华兴书局（Woo Shing Book Store）致闸北中华新路209号新泰祥（Sing Tai Ziang Shop）罗仁伟（Loo Jen-wei）的信函译文。

------------------

罗仁伟先生：

你说你想购买我们的书，但不知道在哪里可以买到，对此我们深感抱歉。但是，如果你认为你发给我们的地址是我们邮寄书籍的地方，我们将立即照办。非常感谢你建议设立私人代理销售我们的书籍。请约定时间和地点，以便我们可以派人去见你，商讨事宜。能否期待你立即回复？你可以将信寄到上次同样的地方。

急切等待你的回复。

上海华兴书局。

2/27

Date March 4, 19 31.

Subject (in full) Letter from one Loong Noong (龍農) addressed to the
proprietor Wong (王) of the Chi Tah Tea Leaf Shop
(吉泰茶莊), 763 Connaught Road. (Jiangnan Bookstore).

Made by D. I. Ross Forwarded by Jho Valentain, Supt.

I forward herewith, together with
translation, a letter dated Shanghai March 3, 1931,
from one Loong Noong (龍農), Foochow and Shantung
Roads, addressed to the proprietor Wong (王) of the
Chi Tah Tea-leaf Shop, No.763 Connaught Road. From
the contents of the letter, which is self explanatory,
it will be seen that the raid on the premises by the
Police on March 1, 1931, has already been circulated.
Loong Noong is in all possibility connected
with the Kiangnan Book Store (江南書局), which,
according to an address found at 763 Connaught Road,
is situated at Foochow and Shantung Roads.
This letter was intercepted by the Police
of Gordon Road Station.

D. I.

D. C. (Cr. & Sp. Branches).

Notes:
The Kiangnan Bookstore, 165 Shantung Road, was sealed
by the Judicial Police on March 4, 1931. A Warrant has
been issued at the request of the Soongwu Military Headquarters
for the arrest of the manager Te Foh Nyien (戴伯年) on a
charge of propagating communism.

(批：See file D. 1939.)
SI, Please explain the reason for
sealing No. 165 Shantung Road, and the
legal process by which the sealing orders
were obtained or issued.
J.R.
5:8:4.

主题（全称）龙农（Loong Noong）致康纳路763号吉泰茶庄（Chi Tah Tea Leaf Shop）（江南书局）店主王（Wong）的信函。

由警探长罗斯（D. I. Ross）呈报 转呈人 乔·瓦伦丁巡官（Jho Valentain, Supt.）

现随函附上1931年3月3日由福州路山东路口的龙农（Loong Noong）致康纳路763号吉泰茶庄店主王（Wong）的信函及其译文。从这封信的内容（自明）可以看出，警方于1931年3月1日对该处所的搜查消息已经传开。龙农极有可能与江南书局（Kiangnan Book Store）有关联，根据在康纳路763号发现的一个地址，该局位于福州路和山东路。
这封信被戈登路巡捕房的警方截获。

警探长

副督察长（刑事及特别股）。

山东路165号的江南书局已于1931年3月4日被司法警察查封。应淞沪警备司令部之请，已签发逮捕经理戴伯年（Te Foh Nyien）的 warrant（逮捕令），指控其宣传共产主义。

(批：见档案 D. 1939.)

page_data.en:
Translation of a letter dated March 3, 1931, from
one Loong Noong (龍農 ), Foochow and Shantung
Roads addressed to the Proprietor Wong (王 ) of the
Chi Tah Tea-Leaf Shop (吉泰茶莊), 763 Connaught Road.

----

3/3/31

Dear Proprietor Wong:

We have been repeatedly trapped
into trouble by our enemies with the result that you
are also implicated into it, for which we are exceedingly
sorry. Apart from suspending our business for the time
being, we have decided to complain to the Court. We
write you this letter to express our regret, and on the
other hand request you to be kind enough to keep any
letters you may receive for us. Of course you are also
asked to be the custodian of the belongings of my sister
and when we have got redress of our grievances at the
Court we will call on you and tender you our sincerest
apologies and at the same time take back all the things.

With best regards,

Loong Noong.
page_data.zh:
1931年3月3日，由福州路山东路口的龙农（Loong Noong）致康纳路763号吉泰茶庄（Chi Tah Tea-Leaf Shop）店主王（Wong）的信函译文。

----

31.3.3

亲爱的王店主：

我们屡遭敌人陷害，导致你也受牵连，对此我们深感抱歉。除了暂时停止营业外，我们决定向法院申诉。我们写这封信是为了表达我们的歉意，另一方面请求你好心代为保管可能收到的给我们的信件。当然，也请你代为保管我妹妹的物品，当我们在法院得到伸冤后，我们将拜访你，致以最诚挚的歉意，同时取回所有物品。

此致问候，

龙农。

page_data.en:
Translation of a circular letter dated February 9,
1931, addressed to the Woo Shing Bookstore, Connaught
Road, from the Ma Kong Min Chun Library (馬公民春圖書館),
Amoy.

-----------------

Dear Sir,

Our library having been recently established,
it is therefore necessary for us to get as many good
books as possible for public reading. As the
literature published by your book store, is known to
have a wide circulation among numerous readers, we,
therefore, ask you to send us one copy each of the
old and new catalogues. Please also inform us
whether there is any special discount granted to
purchasers.

(Sd. & Chopped)
Seal of Ming Chun Library, Makong,
established by the Dong Kuan Hsien.
9/2/31.

-----------------

敬启者：

敝馆最近成立，因此有必要尽可能多地获取好书以供公众阅读。鉴于贵书店出版的文献在众多读者中广为流传，故恳请惠赐新旧目录各一份。并请告知是否对购书者给予特别折扣。

（签名并盖章）

REPORT
Date March 4, 1931.

Subject (in full) Report on the Woo Shing Book Store (華興書局), suspected communist organ.

Made by D. I. Ross Forwarded by Tho Robertson, Supt

With reference to despatch No.5297 from the Shanghai Special District Court and Search Warrant No.1744 issued at the request of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai on the subject of the above, I have to report that diligent enquiries made by this office finally located the Woo Shing Book Store in the upstairs front room of a tea leaf shop at No.763 Connaught Road. On March 1, 1931 the place in question was visited by detectives attached to Gordon Road Station. No one was present at the time of the Police visit and a search of the room failed to reveal anything of incriminating nature beyond a wooden chop bearing the characters "Acknowledgment of Receipt Woo Shing Book Store" (華興書局) and a piece of paper inscribed as follows:
Kiangnan Bookstore (江南書局), Foochow and Shantung Roads----
1186 S Wen Li (斯文里), Tatung and Sinza Roads ---Li Ki-tsuan (李岐瞻). According to the female occupant of the tea hong, named Wong Hai Poh (王海樸), the Woo Shing Book Store was established in the adjoining house, No.762 Connaught Road in September 1929 and removed to 763 Connaught Road in May 1930, where it remained until January, 1931, when it was closed down. The present occupant of the room, where the chop was found, she stated, is a girl student named Sung Yong Fong (宋榮芳), who had been residing there for the past two weeks, but has been absent since February 28. I may mention here that Wong Hai Poh, during the course of the interview, contradicted herself on several occasions and that the information imparted by her should be taken with a certain amount of reserve.
A watch is being maintained on the premises by Gordon Road Station pending the return of Sung Yong Fong.

关于上海特区法院发出的第5297号公函以及应大上海市政府要求就上述事项签发的第1744号搜查令，本局经勤勉调查，最终在康纳路763号一家茶叶店楼上的前间找到了华兴书局。1931年3月1日，隶属于戈登路站的侦探探访了该处。警方到访时屋内无人，对该房间的检查除了一枚刻有“华兴书局收讫”字样的木章和一张写有以下内容的纸条外，未发现任何具有罪证性质的物品：

斯文里1186号，大同路与新闸路 ---李岐瞻。据该茶号的 female occupant（女性住户/经营者），名为王海樸者称，华兴书局于1929年9月在隔壁康纳路762号成立，并于1930年5月迁至康纳路763号，一直营业至1931年1月停业。她说，发现木章的房间目前的居住者是一名名叫宋荣芳的女学生，她在过去两周一直住在那里，但自2月28日起便不在。在此需提及，王海樸在谈话过程中数次自相矛盾，因此对她提供的信息应持保留态度。

opposite the house in question acting in a suspicious manner.
With the departure of the Police from the premises, he walked
away hurriedly in an easterly direction along Connaught Road.
A watch kept on his movements led to No.132 Chang Loh Li
(長樂里), Chang An Road, Chapel, which he entered.
In connection with this matter enquiries among the various
book stores on Foochow Road elicit the information that all
pro-communistic publications which have hitherto appeared on
the market were in practically every instance supplied
through the medium of the Woo Shing Book Store. It was also
ascertained that the literature in question was forwarded through
the post and repeated attempts made by certain book stores
to make a personal visit to the Woo Shing Book Store were
without success.
In view of the foregoing and in the absence of any
signboard or any other visible means of identification, it can be
safely stated that the room at No.763 Connaught Road was being
used as a communication office for the dissemination of
communist propaganda.

No. 5497. February 10, 1931.

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sir,

I am in receipt of a despatch from the Propaganda Department of the Executive Committee of the Shanghai Special District Koumintang to the following effect:-

"We are in receipt of a confidential instruction from the Central Propaganda Bureau to the following effect: 'By reviewing its catalogue, which was seized by the Honan Provincial Government and transmitted to us through the Administrative Yuan, we are under the impression that the Wo Sing Book Store, situate at the east end of Connaught Road, Shanghai, is the propaganda organ of the communists, for having published communistic literatures, such as, Linin's "Two Policies" and many others. Therefore, apart from writing to the State Council for issuance of necessary instructions to the military and police authorities in Shanghai and to the Shanghai Special District Court to seal up the said book store; and apart from instructing various Koumintang Headquarters, Propaganda Department, and the Postal Matters Censors to suppress and to seize such reactionary literatures, we have to instruct that the military and police authorities at Shanghai and the Shanghai Special District Court be approached with a view to having the said book store sealed.' In compliance with the instructions, we have apart from communicating with the Headquarters of the
